Ben —

See inline suggestions below (tracked in the attached spreadsheet). Key legal points:

1) Insurance offset: we should accept a limited netting approach only if Acme agrees to: (a) provide proof of claim/subrogation attempts, and (b) cap any insurer credit at the same recovery amount captured by the cap (i.e., not create a windfall). Proposed text: "Recoveries from insurance shall not reduce Redwood's liability under this Agreement unless Customer provides written evidence of payment and the Parties agree the recovery directly relates to the same loss."

2) Annualized cap: commercial compromise = prior 12 months' fees (as they requested) but with a multiple floor (e.g., 1x prior 12 months OR a minimum of $250k) to protect against small initial spends.

3) Consequential damages carve-outs: accept IP infringement carve-out. For data-related carve-outs, propose a tiered approach:
  - For Customer data breaches caused by Customer negligence: exclude from consequential carve-out.
  - For cloud-provider/3rd-party incidents affecting Redwood runtime: limit exposure to the annualized cap and require mitigation steps.

I'll mark the exact language in the attachment (liability-offset-model.xlsx).

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Ben / team —

Agree with Laura's baseline. A couple of commercial suggestions to close quickly:

- Offer customer the prior 12 months' fees cap (their ask) but include an explicit annual reset clause that looks back every 12 months from the date of the loss. That gives them the predictability and lets us avoid an unbounded cumulative cap.
- Where the customer requests insurance offset (netting), offer a middle-ground: allow netting for first-party insurance only and require a limit that netting cannot reduce Redwood's cap below 50% of the stated cap for any single event.
- For consequential damages: propose a short schedule listing specific carve-outs we will accept (IP infringement, third-party claims for bodily injury if applicable) and explicitly exclude data availability/performance/outages from consequential carve-outs (i.e., we treat those under service credits).

If Ben agrees, I can prepare a redline to send to Acme.

Marissa Cole

Priya —

Thanks for the redlines and patience while we reviewed. We've attached a short summary (redline-summary-ben-20261029.pdf) and a proposed compromise below:

Proposal (summary):
- Cap: "Customer's aggregate liability for claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) $250,000."
- Insurance offset: allow netting of first-party insurance recoveries only if Customer provides evidence of payment; insurance recoveries from third-party subrogation shall not automatically reduce Redwood's cap.
- Consequential damages: Redwood will accept carve-out for IP infringement and for third-party bodily injury claims limited to the extent caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Loss of data or availability will be treated under the service levels and remedies (service credits) and are not included in "consequential damages" carve-outs.

Please see the attached PDF for tracked language and our suggested redlines. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Priya / Daniel —

Thanks — we can accommodate the asks with narrow clarifications. Final proposed language below (legal):

1) Cap: "Customer's aggregate liability for all claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood during the twelve (12) months prior to the event giving rise to the claim, or (ii) the product of (monthly recurring fees at time of claim x 1.0)." This preserves a usage-linked floor while honoring the 12-month lookback.

2) Insurance & waterfall: "Recoveries from Customer's first-party insurance shall be taken into account only after the Parties have exhausted contractual remedies (including service credits). Any insurer payment shall be evidenced in writing and shall reduce Redwood's liability under the Agreement only to the extent it directly compensates the same loss."

3) Incident attribution process: 30-day good-faith investigation window. If attribution remains disputed after 30 days, Parties agree to binding escalation to an independent third-party technical arbiter with costs split equally.

We believe this resolves the procurement and engineering concerns while protecting Redwood from disproportionate exposure. If Acme agrees, Marissa / Ben — please proceed to update the redline and coordinate a final sign-off call.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
